DEFENDANT -

By virtue of a Writ of Execution in the above stated action to me directed, I shall expose for sale at public venue at the Salem County Courthouse, situated at No. 92 Market Street, in the City of Salem, New Jersey on
Monday,
December 14, 2026
at
2 o’clock
in the afternoon, ALL the following lot, tract or parcel of land and premises, situate, lying and being in the Township of Pittsgrove, in the County of Salem and State of New Jersey, bounded and described as follows:
Municipality: Pittsgrove
County of Salem
State of New Jersey
Street and Street No.: 20 Central Avenue Pittsgrove, NJ 08318 with a mailing address of 20 Central Avenue Elmer, NJ 08318
Tax Block and Lot No.: Block 2501, Lot 18
Dimensions of Lot (approximately): 100.75ft x 302.25ft x 100.75ft x 302.25ft
Nearest Cross Street: Approximately 416.06ft to nearest cross street known as Gershal Avenue
A full legal description can be found in the Office of the Clerk of Salem County in Deed Book 4636 at Page 247.
The approximate amount of the judgment to be satisfied by said sale is the sum of $345,389.10 together with the costs of this sale.
The approximate upset price is $371,715.43.
The upset price may be subject to further Orders of additional sums.
Occupancy Status: Borrower Occupied
Pursuant to a municipal Tax Search July 29,2026.
Subject to: 2026 3rd quarter taxes due 8/1/2026, $1,908.99 Open; Grace Period Extended to 8/31/2026
2026 4th quarter taxes due 11/1/2026,$1,908.98 Open
Terms of Sale: 20% of bid in cash, certified check or cashiers check from the successful bidder upon conclusion of sale. The Sheriff’s Office cash limit is $1,000.00 The balance is due within 30 days of the date of sale.
Surplus Money:
If after the sale and satisfaction of the mortgage debt, including costs and expenses, there remains any surplus money, the money will be deposited into the Superior Court Trust Fund and any person claiming the surplus, or any part thereof, may file a motion pursuant to the Court Rules 4:64-3 and 4:57-2 stating the nature and extent of that person’s claim and asking for an order directing payment of the surplus money. The Sheriff or other person conducting the sale will have information regarding the surplus, if any.
The Sheriff reserves the right to adjourn the sale without further notice through publication.
Hill Wallack LLP
, Attorneys for Plaintiff
Charles M. Miller, Sheriff
